name: Neural Rendering
author: jlrouzies-fr
description:
Neural Rendering (DLSS 5) in your games, as ReShade add-ons.
Pick your graphics card at the top right.
license: Each project keeps its own license (see Credits)

options.label: NVIDIA
options.title: NVIDIA RTX 20 to 50: games without DLSS
options.description:
Needs an NVIDIA RTX 20, 30, 40 or 50 card.
For 64-bit DirectX games WITHOUT a DLSS option. Download: about 150 MB.
Not sure which tab? Does the game have a DLSS option? Yes: NVIDIA + DLSS. No: NVIDIA.
It installs 2 add-ons, and both are needed:
1. dlss5-feed hands the game picture to DLSS.
2. renodx-dlss5 does the neural rendering.
Then, in ReShade:
1. Put SuperDepth3D (if you use it) at the top.
2. Turn on LUMENITE: Kernel 2.0 below it.
3. Turn on DLSS5_Feed below the Kernel.
4. In the DLSS 5 Neural Rendering panel, turn it on.
5. Nothing changes? Try turning the game's MSAA off.
GPU Selector sets DLSS5_MV_PROVIDER=3 and IMAGE_SPACE=1 for you, if they are not set yet.

Have NVIDIA and AMD cards? Install both tabs. Each game loads the one for the GPU it uses.
options.author: jlrouzies-fr and Krish

options.label: NVIDIA + DLSS
options.title: NVIDIA RTX 20 to 50: games that have DLSS
options.description:
Needs an NVIDIA RTX 20, 30, 40 or 50 card.
For 64-bit DX11 or DX12 games WITH a DLSS option.
Not sure which tab? Does the game have a DLSS option? Yes: NVIDIA + DLSS. No: NVIDIA.
It installs 1 add-on: renodx-dlss5.
The game's own DLSS does the rest.
1. Turn DLSS on in the game.
2. In ReShade, open the DLSS 5 Neural Rendering panel.
3. Turn it on (F6).
4. Its file (nvngx_dlssnr.dll) sits next to the game only while it runs.

Have NVIDIA and AMD cards? Install both tabs. Each game loads the one for the GPU it uses.
options.author: Krish (RenoDX)

options.label: AMD
options.title: AMD Radeon RX 6000 / 7000 / 9000: DX11 works best
options.description:
Needs an AMD Radeon RX 6000, 7000 or 9000 card.
Tested on RX 9000. RX 6000 and 7000 should work, but are untested.
For 64-bit games. Download: about 210 MB.
Works best in DX11. DX12 works, but is not the way the author recommends. DX10, Vulkan and OpenGL are experimental.
1. Your AMD driver must be current (it has HIP 7). RX 6000 also needs AMD's HIP SDK 7.2.
2. The runtime and weights sit next to the game only while it runs.
3. Put AMD Neural Feed at the very top, above all other effects.
4. Put SuperDepth3D (if you use it) below it.
5. Put LUMENITE: Kernel 2.0 below SuperDepth3D, above your other effects.
6. Tick all three.
7. Turn on AMD Neural Rendering (Ctrl+End).
GPU Selector sets AMDNR_MV_PROVIDER=3 and IMAGE_SPACE=1 for you, if they are not set yet.

Have NVIDIA and AMD cards? Install both tabs. Each game loads the one for the GPU it uses.
